```javascript
      // A refused delete (409 while a job runs, #40) is shown in the dialog. The
      // page-level error line sits behind the overlay, where it read as nothing.
      // The DELETE is answered here, so no collection is touched.
      const busyMessage = "An ingest job is running for this collection ('Owned', job 0wned40). Delete the collection after the job finishes.";
      await s.page.setRequestInterception(true);
      s.page.on('request', request => {
        if (request.method() === 'DELETE' && new URL(request.url()).pathname.startsWith('/api/collections/')) {
          return request.respond({ status: 409, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ error: { code: 'COLLECTION_BUSY', message: busyMessage, detail: { job_kind: 'ingest', job_id: '0wned40' } } }) });
        }
        return request.continue();
      });
      const target = await s.page.evaluate(() => {
        const el = [...document.querySelectorAll('input')].find(i => !i.type || i.type === 'text');
        const name = el.placeholder;
        Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value').set.call(el, name);
        el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
        return name;
      });
      await sleep(200);
      const deletes = s.api.filter(x => x.method === 'DELETE').length;
      await s.page.evaluate(() => {
        const btn = [...document.querySelectorAll('button')]
          .find(b => b.textContent.trim() === 'Delete' && b.className.includes('bg-red-600'));
        if (btn && !btn.disabled) btn.click();
      });
      await sleep(900);
      const refused = await s.page.evaluate(() => {
        const dialog = [...document.querySelectorAll('h2')].find(h => h.textContent.trim() === 'Delete Collection');
        const box = dialog && dialog.parentElement;
        const alert = box && box.querySelector('[role=alert]');
        return { open: !!dialog, alert: alert ? alert.textContent : null };
      });
      r.check('a refused delete sends one DELETE', s.api.filter(x => x.method === 'DELETE').length === deletes + 1);
      r.check('a refused delete keeps the dialog open and shows the message in it',
              refused.open && refused.alert === busyMessage, JSON.stringify(refused));
      const listed = await s.page.evaluate(t => [...document.querySelectorAll('tbody td')].some(td => td.textContent.trim() === t), target);
      r.check('the refused collection is still listed', listed, target);
      await clickByText(s.page, 'Cancel'); await sleep(200);
      await s.page.evaluate(() => {
        const b = [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].find(x => x.textContent.trim() === 'Delete');
        if (b) b.click();
      });
      await sleep(300);
      r.check('cancelling clears the message for the next attempt',
              await s.page.evaluate(() => !document.querySelector('[role=alert]')));
    }
    await s.ctx.close();
  }

  // ── refused creates and failed collection lists (#379) ───────────────────
  // A refused create went to the page-level error line behind the modal's
  // overlay, so it looked like nothing happened, and a failed GET /collections
  // was swallowed, so an outage looked like "no collections". The POSTs and the
  // failing lists are answered here, so no collection is created.
  r.section('refused creates and failed collection lists (#379)');
  {
    const LIST_FAIL = 'Synthetic list failure (#379).';
    const LIST_MESSAGE = 'Could not load the collections: ' + LIST_FAIL;
    const EXISTS = "Collection 'VfyRefused379' already exists.";
    const listFailure = { status: 503, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ error: { code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE', message: LIST_FAIL, detail: null } }) };
    const refusal = { status: 409, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ error: { code: 'COLLECTION_EXISTS', message: EXISTS, detail: null } }) };
    const accepted = { status: 201, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ name: 'VfyRefused379', status: 'created' }) };
    const alerts = page => page.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('[role=alert]')].map(a => a.textContent.trim()));
    // The New Collection modal, and the alert inside it, if any.
    const modal = page => page.evaluate(() => {
      const h = [...document.querySelectorAll('h2')].find(x => x.textContent.trim() === 'New Collection');
      const box = h && h.parentElement;
      const alert = box && box.querySelector('[role=alert]');
      return { open: !!h, alert: alert ? alert.textContent.trim() : null };
    });
    // Answers GET and POST /api/collections as the test's current modes say.
    async function stub(s) {
      const mode = { list: 'pass', post: 'refuse' };
      await s.page.setRequestInterception(true);
      s.page.on('request', request => {
        if (new URL(request.url()).pathname !== '/api/collections') return request.continue();
        if (request.method() === 'GET' && mode.list === 'fail') return request.respond(listFailure);
        if (request.method() === 'POST') return request.respond(mode.post === 'refuse' ? refusal : accepted);
        return request.continue();
      });
      return mode;
    }
    const posts = s => s.api.filter(x => x.method === 'POST' && x.url === '/api/collections').length;

    // A failed list on each page that loads one.
    for (const path of ['/collections', '/import', '/qa', '/goldstandard']) {
      const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'engineer');
      try {
        const mode = await stub(s);
        mode.list = 'fail';
        await s.page.goto(BASE + path, { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
        const shown = await alerts(s.page);
        r.check(`${path}: a failed collection list is shown as an alert`, shown.includes(LIST_MESSAGE), JSON.stringify(shown));
        r.check(`${path}: a failed collection list causes no React page errors`, !s.errors.some(e => e.startsWith('pageerror:')), s.errors.slice(0, 2).join(' | '));
      } finally { await s.ctx.close(); }
    }

    // Collections page: a refused create, then a successful one, which also
    // reloads the list and clears the failed-list message.
    {
      const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'engineer');
      try {
        const mode = await stub(s);
        mode.list = 'fail';
        await s.page.goto(BASE + '/collections', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
        await clickByText(s.page, '+ New Collection'); await sleep(300);
        await setValue(s.page, "() => document.querySelector('input[placeholder=Name]')", 'VfyRefused379');
        const before = posts(s);
        await clickByText(s.page, 'Create'); await sleep(900);
        const refused = await modal(s.page);
        r.check('Collections: a refused create sends one POST', posts(s) === before + 1);
        r.check('Collections: a refused create keeps the modal open and shows the message in it',
                refused.open && refused.alert === EXISTS, JSON.stringify(refused));
        await clickByText(s.page, 'Cancel'); await sleep(200);
        await clickByText(s.page, '+ New Collection'); await sleep(300);
        const reopened = await modal(s.page);
        r.check('Collections: cancelling clears the message for the next attempt', reopened.open && reopened.alert === null, JSON.stringify(reopened));
        await clickByText(s.page, 'Create'); await sleep(900);
        mode.post = 'accept'; mode.list = 'pass';
        await clickByText(s.page, 'Create'); await sleep(1500);
        const done = await modal(s.page);
        r.check('Collections: a successful create closes the modal', !done.open, JSON.stringify(done));
        const after = await alerts(s.page);
        r.check('Collections: the next successful list clears the failed-list message', !after.includes(LIST_MESSAGE), JSON.stringify(after));
        await clickByText(s.page, '+ New Collection'); await sleep(300);
        const fresh = await modal(s.page);
        r.check('Collections: a successful create clears the message for the next attempt', fresh.open && fresh.alert === null, JSON.stringify(fresh));
        r.check('Collections create fixtures cause no React page errors', !s.errors.some(e => e.startsWith('pageerror:')), s.errors.slice(0, 2).join(' | '));
      } finally { await s.ctx.close(); }
    }

    // Import page "+ New": a refused create, then a successful one whose list
    // reload fails, which is a list error, not a refused create.
    {
      const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'engineer');
      try {
        const mode = await stub(s);
        await s.page.goto(BASE + '/import', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
        await clickByText(s.page, '+ New'); await sleep(300);
        await setValue(s.page, "() => document.querySelector('input[placeholder=\"Collection name\"]')", 'VfyRefused379');
        const before = posts(s);
        await clickByText(s.page, 'Create'); await sleep(900);
        const refused = await modal(s.page);
        r.check('Import: a refused create sends one POST', posts(s) === before + 1);
        r.check('Import: a refused create keeps the modal open and shows the message in it',
                refused.open && refused.alert === EXISTS, JSON.stringify(refused));
        await clickByText(s.page, 'Cancel'); await sleep(200);
        await clickByText(s.page, '+ New'); await sleep(300);
        const reopened = await modal(s.page);
        r.check('Import: cancelling clears the message for the next attempt', reopened.open && reopened.alert === null, JSON.stringify(reopened));
        await setValue(s.page, "() => document.querySelector('input[placeholder=\"Collection name\"]')", 'VfyRefused379');
        await clickByText(s.page, 'Create'); await sleep(900);
        mode.post = 'accept'; mode.list = 'fail';
        await clickByText(s.page, 'Create'); await sleep(1500);
        const done = await modal(s.page);
        const after = await alerts(s.page);
        r.check('Import: a successful create closes the modal even when the list reload fails', !done.open, JSON.stringify(done));
        r.check('Import: a failed reload after a create is shown as a failed list', after.includes(LIST_MESSAGE), JSON.stringify(after));
        await clickByText(s.page, '+ New'); await sleep(300);
        const fresh = await modal(s.page);
        r.check('Import: a successful create clears the message for the next attempt', fresh.open && fresh.alert === null, JSON.stringify(fresh));
        r.check('Import create fixtures cause no React page errors', !s.errors.some(e => e.startsWith('pageerror:')), s.errors.slice(0, 2).join(' | '));
      } finally { await s.ctx.close(); }
    }
  }

  // ── the created name as stored (#372) ──────────────────────────────────────
  // Weaviate capitalises a collection's first letter, and the list shows that
  // name. The Import page selected the typed name, which matched no option, so
  // React showed the first option instead while uploads went to the typed name.
  // /api/collections is answered here, the list with a decoy first, so that
  // fallback can't pass the check; nothing is created on the stack.
  r.section('the created name as stored (#372)');
  {
    const TYPED = 'vfySpelling372', STORED = 'VfySpelling372', DECOY = 'VfyDecoy372';
    const info = name => ({ name, object_count: 0, index_type: 'hnsw', distance_metric: 'cosine', created_at: null, hnsw_config: null });
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'engineer');
    try {
      await s.page.setRequestInterception(true);
      let created = false;
      s.page.on('request', request => {
        if (new URL(request.url()).pathname !== '/api/collections') return request.continue();
        if (request.method() === 'POST') {
          created = true;
          return request.respond({ status: 201, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ name: STORED, status: 'created' }) });
        }
        const list = created ? [info(DECOY), info(STORED)] : [info(DECOY)];
        return request.respond({ status: 200, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ collections: list }) });
      });
      await s.page.goto(BASE + '/import', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
      await clickByText(s.page, '+ New'); await sleep(300);
      await setValue(s.page, "() => document.querySelector('input[placeholder=\"Collection name\"]')", TYPED);
      await clickByText(s.page, 'Create'); await sleep(1500);
      const selected = await s.page.evaluate(() => {
        const label = [...document.querySelectorAll('label')].find(x => x.textContent.trim() === 'Collection');
        const select = label && label.parentElement.querySelector('select');
        return select ? { value: select.value, options: [...select.options].map(o => o.value) } : null;
      });
      r.check('Import: after "+ New", the selector holds the created collection as stored',
              !!selected && selected.value === STORED, JSON.stringify(selected));
      r.check('Import stored-name fixture causes no React page errors', !s.errors.some(e => e.startsWith('pageerror:')), s.errors.slice(0, 2).join(' | '));
    } finally { await s.ctx.close(); }
  }

  // ── upload size limit ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // The Import page refuses a selection over the proxy's limit before sending.
  // The file is sparse: it reports 513 MB but occupies no disk, and the check
  // must stop it before the browser ever reads it. See issue #21.
  r.section('upload size limit');
  {
    const fs = require('fs');
    const big = '/tmp/vfy-oversize-upload.txt';
    fs.closeSync(fs.openSync(big, 'w'));
    fs.truncateSync(big, 513 * 1024 * 1024);
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'developer');
    await s.page.goto(BASE + '/import', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
    const hint = await bodyText(s.page);
    r.check('the drop zone states the upload limit', hint.includes('up to 512 MB per upload'));
    const input = await s.page.$('#file-input');
    await input.uploadFile(big);
    await sleep(500);
    const posts = () => s.api.filter(x => x.method === 'POST' && x.url.includes('/ingest/upload')).length;
    const before = posts();
    const clicked = await clickByText(s.page, 'Start Ingest');
    await sleep(900);
    const text = await bodyText(s.page);
    r.check('an oversize selection is refused with the limit named',
            clicked && text.includes('one upload can be at most 512 MB'),
            clicked ? text.slice(0, 160) : 'Start Ingest button not found');
    r.check('an oversize selection sends no upload', posts() === before);
    r.check('no console errors on the import page', s.errors.length === 0, s.errors.slice(0, 2).join(' | '));
    fs.unlinkSync(big);
    await s.ctx.close();
  }

  // ── import file types (#291) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  // The picker offers JSON Lines, plain and gzipped, and the hint names it.
  r.section('import file types');
  {
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'developer');
    try {
      await s.page.goto(BASE + '/import', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
      const accept = await s.page.evaluate(() => {
        const input = document.querySelector('#file-input');
        return input ? input.getAttribute('accept') : null;
      });
      r.check('the file picker accepts .jsonl and .jsonl.gz',
              accept === '.pdf,.docx,.txt,.md,.csv,.json,.jsonl,.jsonl.gz,.zip', String(accept));
      const hint = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('the drop zone hint names JSONL among the types',
              hint.includes('PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD, CSV, JSON, JSONL, ZIP · up to 512 MB per upload'),
              hint.slice(0, 200));
    } finally {
      await s.ctx.close();
    }
  }

  // ── import errors (#290) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // A truncated ZIP once ended in a plain-text 500 that the page could only
  // show as "HTTP 500", and a failing status poll was ignored.
  r.section('import error messages');
  {
    const fs = require('fs');
    const truncated = '/tmp/vfy-truncated.zip';
    // A local file header and nothing after it: no central directory.
    fs.writeFileSync(truncated, Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('PK\x03\x04', 'latin1'), Buffer.alloc(64, 0x61)]));
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'developer');
    try {
      await s.page.goto(BASE + '/import', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
      const input = await s.page.$('#file-input');
      await input.uploadFile(truncated);
      await sleep(300);
      const clicked = await clickByText(s.page, 'Start Ingest');
      await sleep(2500);
      const text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check("a truncated ZIP shows the API's message, not HTTP 500",
              clicked && text.includes("is damaged and can't be read") && !text.includes('HTTP 500'),
              clicked ? text.slice(0, 200) : 'Start Ingest button not found');
    } finally {
      fs.unlinkSync(truncated);
      await s.ctx.close();
    }
  }
  {
    const fs = require('fs');
    const small = '/tmp/vfy-poll.txt';
    fs.writeFileSync(small, 'Polling fixture.\n');
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'developer');
    await s.page.setRequestInterception(true);
    s.page.on('request', request => {
      const path = new URL(request.url()).pathname;
      if (path === '/api/ingest/upload' && request.method() === 'POST')
        return request.respond({ status: 202, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ job_id: 'vfypoll1', status: 'queued', files_queued: 1, collection: 'x' }) });
      if (path === '/api/ingest/job/vfypoll1')
        return request.respond({ status: 500, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ error: { code: 'X', message: 'Synthetic status failure.', detail: null } }) });
      return request.continue();
    });
    try {
      await s.page.goto(BASE + '/import', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
      const input = await s.page.$('#file-input');
      await input.uploadFile(small);
      await sleep(300);
      const clicked = await clickByText(s.page, 'Start Ingest');
      await sleep(4500);
      const text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('a failing status poll is shown, not ignored',
              clicked && text.includes("Could not check the import's progress: Synthetic status failure."),
              clicked ? text.slice(0, 200) : 'Start Ingest button not found');
      r.check('import error fixtures cause no React page errors', !s.errors.some(e => e.startsWith('pageerror:')));
    } finally {
      fs.unlinkSync(small);
      await s.ctx.close();
    }
  }
  // A poll error is cleared by a new ingest and by the next successful poll
  // (#298). Job A's polls always fail; job B's first poll fails, then it
  // completes. Polls run every 3 s.
  {
    const fs = require('fs');
    const small = '/tmp/vfy-poll-clear.txt';
    fs.writeFileSync(small, 'Polling fixture.\n');
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'developer');
    const failure = JSON.stringify({ error: { code: 'X', message: 'Synthetic status failure.', detail: null } });
    let uploads = 0, pollsB = 0;
    await s.page.setRequestInterception(true);
    s.page.on('request', request => {
      const path = new URL(request.url()).pathname;
      if (path === '/api/ingest/upload' && request.method() === 'POST') {
        uploads += 1;
        const job = uploads === 1 ? 'vfyclrA' : 'vfyclrB';
        return request.respond({ status: 202, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ job_id: job, status: 'queued', files_queued: 1, collection: 'x' }) });
      }
      if (path === '/api/ingest/job/vfyclrA')
        return request.respond({ status: 500, contentType: 'application/json', body: failure });
      if (path === '/api/ingest/job/vfyclrB') {
        pollsB += 1;
        if (pollsB === 1) return request.respond({ status: 500, contentType: 'application/json', body: failure });
        return request.respond({ status: 200, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ job_id: 'vfyclrB', status: 'completed', files_total: 1, files_completed: 1, files_failed: 0, chunks_stored: 2, chunks_replaced: 0, errors: [], skipped: [] }) });
      }
      return request.continue();
    });
    const shown = text => text.includes("Could not check the import's progress: Synthetic status failure.");
    try {
      await s.page.goto(BASE + '/import', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
      const input = await s.page.$('#file-input');
      await input.uploadFile(small);
      await sleep(300);
      const first = await clickByText(s.page, 'Start Ingest');
      await sleep(4500);                       // job A's first poll has failed
      const before = shown(await bodyText(s.page));
      const second = await clickByText(s.page, 'Start Ingest');
      await sleep(1000);                       // job B accepted, not yet polled
      const afterNew = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('a new ingest clears a poll error',
              first && second && before && uploads === 2 && !shown(afterNew),
              `clicked=${first},${second} shown-before=${before} uploads=${uploads} after: ${afterNew.slice(0, 160)}`);
      await sleep(2700);                       // job B's first poll has failed
      const failedAgain = shown(await bodyText(s.page));
      await sleep(3000);                       // job B's second poll has succeeded
      const afterPoll = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('the next successful poll clears a poll error',
              failedAgain && pollsB >= 2 && !shown(afterPoll),
              `shown-after-B's-first-poll=${failedAgain} B-polls=${pollsB} after: ${afterPoll.slice(0, 160)}`);
    } finally {
      fs.unlinkSync(small);
      await s.ctx.close();
    }
  }

  // ── import job feedback (#394) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  // The job ID was never shown, nothing appeared until the first poll 3 s
  // after the upload was accepted, and "Start Ingest" with no collection
  // selected did nothing. The collection list, the upload and the polls are
  // stubbed: the first poll fails, later ones answer a running job.
  r.section('import job feedback (#394)');
  {
    const fs = require('fs');
    const small = '/tmp/vfy-job-feedback.txt';
    fs.writeFileSync(small, 'Job feedback fixture.\n');
    const jobId = 'vfyjob394';
    const QUEUED = 'Waiting for the first progress update queued';
    const NO_COLLECTION = 'Choose a collection to import into first. Use + New to create one.';
    const POLL_FAIL = "Could not check the import's progress: Synthetic status failure.";
    const polls = s => s.api.filter(x => x.method === 'GET' && x.url === '/api/ingest/job/' + jobId).length;
    const uploads = s => s.api.filter(x => x.method === 'POST' && x.url === '/api/ingest/upload').length;
    async function stub(s, names) {
      let answered = 0;
      const list = names.map(name => ({ name, object_count: 0, index_type: 'hnsw', distance_metric: 'cosine', created_at: null }));
      await s.page.setRequestInterception(true);
      s.page.on('request', request => {
        const path = new URL(request.url()).pathname;
        if (path === '/api/collections' && request.method() === 'GET')
          return request.respond({ status: 200, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ collections: list }) });
        if (path === '/api/ingest/upload' && request.method() === 'POST')
          return request.respond({ status: 202, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ job_id: jobId, status: 'queued', files_queued: 1, collection: 'VfyJob394' }) });
        if (path === '/api/ingest/job/' + jobId) {
          answered += 1;
          if (answered === 1)
            return request.respond({ status: 500, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ error: { code: 'X', message: 'Synthetic status failure.', detail: null } }) });
          return request.respond({ status: 200, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ job_id: jobId, status: 'running', files_total: 1, files_completed: 0, files_failed: 0, chunks_stored: 0, errors: [], skipped: [] }) });
        }
        return request.continue();
      });
    }
    try {
      {
        const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'developer');
        try {
          await stub(s, ['VfyJob394']);
          await s.page.goto(BASE + '/import', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
          const input = await s.page.$('#file-input');
          await input.uploadFile(small);
          await sleep(300);
          const clicked = await clickByText(s.page, 'Start Ingest');
          await sleep(1000);                     // accepted, not yet polled
          const accepted = await bodyText(s.page);
          r.check('the job ID and a queued panel show as soon as the upload is accepted, before any poll',
                  clicked && uploads(s) === 1 && polls(s) === 0 && accepted.includes('Job ID: ' + jobId) && accepted.includes(QUEUED),
                  `clicked=${clicked} uploads=${uploads(s)} polls=${polls(s)} text: ${accepted.slice(0, 240)}`);
          await sleep(3500);                     // the first poll has failed
          const failed = await bodyText(s.page);
          r.check('a failed first poll keeps the job ID and the queued panel, with the poll error',
                  polls(s) === 1 && failed.includes('Job ID: ' + jobId) && failed.includes(QUEUED) && failed.includes(POLL_FAIL),
                  `polls=${polls(s)} text: ${failed.slice(0, 300)}`);
          await sleep(3000);                     // the second poll has answered
          const running = await bodyText(s.page);
          r.check('the first answered poll replaces the queued panel with progress, and the job ID stays',
                  polls(s) >= 2 && running.includes('Files: 0/1') && running.includes('running') &&
                  !running.includes('Waiting for the first progress update') && running.includes('Job ID: ' + jobId),
                  `polls=${polls(s)} text: ${running.slice(0, 300)}`);
          r.check('import job feedback fixtures cause no React page errors', !s.errors.some(e => e.startsWith('pageerror:')), s.errors.slice(0, 2).join(' | '));
        } finally { await s.ctx.close(); }
      }
      {
        const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'developer');
        try {
          await stub(s, []);
          await s.page.goto(BASE + '/import', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
          const input = await s.page.$('#file-input');
          await input.uploadFile(small);
          await sleep(300);
          const clicked = await clickByText(s.page, 'Start Ingest');
          await sleep(900);
          const text = await bodyText(s.page);
          r.check('"Start Ingest" with no collection selected says so and sends no upload',
                  clicked && uploads(s) === 0 && text.includes(NO_COLLECTION),
                  `clicked=${clicked} uploads=${uploads(s)} text: ${text.slice(0, 240)}`);
          r.check('the no-collection fixture causes no React page errors', !s.errors.some(e => e.startsWith('pageerror:')), s.errors.slice(0, 2).join(' | '));
        } finally { await s.ctx.close(); }
      }
    } finally {
      fs.unlinkSync(small);
    }
  }

  // ── re-ingest progress (#22) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  // The progress panel reports replaced chunks, and the skipped heading no
  // longer claims every skip is an unsupported type: a later file with the
  // same name in one upload is skipped too. Job responses are stubbed.
  r.section('re-ingest progress');
  for (const [replaced, label] of [[3, 'Replaced 3 chunks from a previous version'], [1, 'Replaced 1 chunk from a previous version'], [0, null]]) {
    const fs = require('fs');
    const small = '/tmp/vfy-reingest.txt';
    fs.writeFileSync(small, 'Re-ingest fixture.\n');
    const jobId = 'vfyrein' + replaced;
    const skippedEntry = "u.zip:a/r.txt (replaced by r.txt later in this upload, same name 'a/r.txt')";
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'developer');
    await s.page.setRequestInterception(true);
    s.page.on('request', request => {
      const path = new URL(request.url()).pathname;
      if (path === '/api/ingest/upload' && request.method() === 'POST')
        return request.respond({ status: 202, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ job_id: jobId, status: 'queued', files_queued: 1, collection: 'x' }) });
      if (path === '/api/ingest/job/' + jobId)
        return request.respond({ status: 200, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ job_id: jobId, status: 'completed', files_total: 1, files_completed: 1, files_failed: 0, chunks_stored: 2, errors: [], skipped: [skippedEntry], chunks_replaced: replaced }) });
      return request.continue();
    });
    try {
      await s.page.goto(BASE + '/import', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
      const input = await s.page.$('#file-input');
      await input.uploadFile(small);
      await sleep(300);
      const clicked = await clickByText(s.page, 'Start Ingest');
      await sleep(4500);
      const text = await bodyText(s.page);
      if (label) {
        r.check(`chunks_replaced=${replaced} is shown as "${label}"`, clicked && text.includes(label),
                clicked ? text.slice(0, 240) : 'Start Ingest button not found');
      } else {
        r.check('chunks_replaced=0 shows no replacement line', clicked && text.includes('Chunks stored: 2') && !text.includes('Replaced '),
                clicked ? text.slice(0, 240) : 'Start Ingest button not found');
        r.check('the skipped heading is a plain "1 file skipped:" with the entry\'s own reason',
                text.includes('1 file skipped:') && !text.includes('not a supported type:') && text.includes(skippedEntry),
                text.slice(0, 300));
      }
      r.check(`re-ingest progress fixture (${replaced}) causes no React page errors`, !s.errors.some(e => e.startsWith('pageerror:')));
    } finally {
      fs.unlinkSync(small);
      await s.ctx.close();
    }
  }

  // ── ingest write counts and a delete in progress (#302) ──────────────────
  // The progress panel shows submitted, accepted and stored chunks only when
  // they differ; a clean job and an older record without the counts look as
  // before. An upload refused while its collection is being deleted shows the
  // API's message. Responses are stubbed.
  r.section('ingest write counts');
  const countCases = [
    ['differing counts', { chunks_submitted: 10, chunks_accepted: 10, chunks_stored: 0, status: 'failed', files_completed: 0, files_failed: 1 }, 'Submitted 10 · accepted 10 · stored 0'],
    ['equal counts', { chunks_submitted: 2, chunks_accepted: 2, chunks_stored: 2, status: 'completed', files_completed: 1, files_failed: 0 }, null],
    ['a record without the counts', { chunks_stored: 5, status: 'completed', files_completed: 1, files_failed: 0 }, null],
  ];
  for (const [label, fields, line] of countCases) {
    const fs = require('fs');
    const small = '/tmp/vfy-counts.txt';
    fs.writeFileSync(small, 'Write counts fixture.\n');
    const jobId = 'vfycnt' + countCases.findIndex(c => c[0] === label);
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'developer');
    await s.page.setRequestInterception(true);
    s.page.on('request', request => {
      const path = new URL(request.url()).pathname;
      if (path === '/api/ingest/upload' && request.method() === 'POST')
        return request.respond({ status: 202, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ job_id: jobId, status: 'queued', files_queued: 1, collection: 'x' }) });
      if (path === '/api/ingest/job/' + jobId)
        return request.respond({ status: 200, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ job_id: jobId, files_total: 1, errors: [], skipped: [], chunks_replaced: 0, ...fields }) });
      return request.continue();
    });
    try {
      await s.page.goto(BASE + '/import', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
      const input = await s.page.$('#file-input');
      await input.uploadFile(small);
      await sleep(300);
      const clicked = await clickByText(s.page, 'Start Ingest');
      await sleep(4500);
      const text = await bodyText(s.page);
      if (line) {
        r.check(`${label}: the panel shows "${line}"`, clicked && text.includes(line),
                clicked ? text.slice(0, 240) : 'Start Ingest button not found');
      } else {
        r.check(`${label}: the panel shows no submitted/accepted line`,
                clicked && text.includes(`Chunks stored: ${fields.chunks_stored}`) && !text.includes('Submitted '),
                clicked ? text.slice(0, 240) : 'Start Ingest button not found');
      }
      r.check(`write counts fixture (${label}) causes no React page errors`, !s.errors.some(e => e.startsWith('pageerror:')));
    } finally {
      fs.unlinkSync(small);
      await s.ctx.close();
    }
  }
  {
    const fs = require('fs');
    const small = '/tmp/vfy-deleting.txt';
    fs.writeFileSync(small, 'Deleting fixture.\n');
    const message = "Collection 'VfyGone' is being deleted. Start the job again once the delete finishes; the collection must be created again first.";
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'developer');
    await s.page.setRequestInterception(true);
    s.page.on('request', request => {
      const path = new URL(request.url()).pathname;
      if (path === '/api/ingest/upload' && request.method() === 'POST')
        return request.respond({ status: 409, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ error: { code: 'COLLECTION_DELETING', message, detail: { collection: 'VfyGone' } } }) });
      return request.continue();
    });
    try {
      await s.page.goto(BASE + '/import', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(1500);
      const input = await s.page.$('#file-input');
      await input.uploadFile(small);
      await sleep(300);
      const clicked = await clickByText(s.page, 'Start Ingest');
      await sleep(1500);
      const text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('an upload refused with 409 COLLECTION_DELETING shows its message', clicked && text.includes(message),
              clicked ? text.slice(0, 300) : 'Start Ingest button not found');
    } finally {
      fs.unlinkSync(small);
      await s.ctx.close();
    }
  }

  // ── health dashboard ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  r.section('§10.4 health dashboard');
  {
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'engineer');
    await s.page.goto(BASE + '/health', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(2500);
    const body = await bodyText(s.page);
    const latencies = body.match(/\d+\s*ms/g) || [];
    r.check('per-service latency is shown', latencies.length >= 3, latencies.slice(0, 5).join(' '));
    // Services are labelled by role and model, not by the word "Ollama".
    for (const want of ['Weaviate', 'LLM', 'Embed']) {
      r.check(`the dashboard names ${want}`, new RegExp(want, 'i').test(body));
    }
    if (process.env.RAG_SKIP_SLOW === '1') {
      r.skip('30s auto-refresh', 'needs a 70s observation window');
    } else {
      const t0 = Date.now(); s.api.length = 0;
      await sleep(70000);
      const hits = s.api.filter(x => x.url.includes('/health')).map(x => Math.round((x.at - t0) / 1000));
      const gaps = hits.slice(1).map((v, i) => v - hits[i]);
      r.check('the dashboard refreshes on its own', hits.length >= 2, `polled at t+${hits.join('s, t+')}s`);
      r.check('the interval is about 30s', gaps.length > 0 && gaps.every(g => g >= 25 && g <= 35), `gaps: ${gaps.join(', ')}s`);
    }
    r.check('no console errors on the health page', s.errors.length === 0, s.errors.slice(0, 2).join(' | '));
    await s.ctx.close();
  }

  // ── degraded and unreachable health (#375) ─────────────────────────────────
  // /health answers 503 with its per-service body when a dependency is down. The
  // page must show that body, red for the failing service, keep loading the
  // latency metrics, and say so when health can't be read at all. Each load is
  // driven by hand through the captured 30s refresh, with the answers stubbed.
  r.section('degraded and unreachable health (#375)');
  {
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'engineer');
    await s.page.evaluateOnNewDocument(() => {
      const original = window.setInterval;
      window.setInterval = (fn, delay, ...args) => {
        if (delay === 30000) { window.__ownedHealthRefresh = fn; return 45002; }
        return original(fn, delay, ...args);
      };
    });
    const service = (status, latency_ms, model) => model ? { status, latency_ms, model } : { status, latency_ms };
    const healthBody = (status, embed) => ({
      status,
      services: {
        weaviate: service('ok', 11),
        ollama: { llm: service('ok', 22, 'phi3.5'), embed: service(embed, 33, 'nomic-embed-text') },
      },
      resources: { memory: { status: 'ok', allocated_gb: 11.67, recommended_minimum_gb: 12.0 } },
    });
    const proxyPage = code => `<html><head><title>${code}</title></head><body><center><h1>${code}</h1></center><hr><center>nginx</center></body></html>`;
    const metricsBody = n => ({
      total_records: n,
      retrieval_latency: { p50: 10, p95: 20, p99: 30 },
      llm_latency: { p50: 100, p95: 200, p99: 300 },
      total_latency: { p50: 110, p95: 220, p99: 330 },
      history: Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({ timestamp: new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 9, 1, 0, 0, i)).toISOString(), collection: 'OwnedFixture', retrieval_mode: 'hybrid', retrieval_ms: 10, llm_ms: 100, total_ms: 110 })),
    });
    let mode = 'degraded', loads = 0;
    await s.page.setRequestInterception(true);
    s.page.on('request', request => {
      const path = new URL(request.url()).pathname;
      if (path === '/api/health') {
        if (mode === 'refused') return request.abort('connectionrefused');
        if (mode === 'proxy502') return request.respond({ status: 502, contentType: 'text/html', body: proxyPage('502 Bad Gateway') });
        if (mode === 'html503') return request.respond({ status: 503, contentType: 'text/html', body: proxyPage('503 Service Temporarily Unavailable') });
        const degraded = mode === 'degraded';
        return request.respond({ status: degraded ? 503 : 200, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify(healthBody(degraded ? 'degraded' : 'ok', degraded ? 'error' : 'ok')) });
      }
      if (path === '/api/metrics/latency') {
        loads++;
        return request.respond({ status: 200, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify(metricsBody(loads)) });
      }
      return request.continue();
    });
    // Each service card's label and dot colour; the latency tiles have no dot.
    const cards = () => s.page.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('span.rounded-full.w-2')].map(dot => ({
      label: (dot.parentElement.textContent || '').trim(),
      red: dot.classList.contains('bg-red-500'), green: dot.classList.contains('bg-green-500'),
    })));
    const colours = list => list.map(c => `${c.label}=${c.red ? 'red' : c.green ? 'green' : '?'}`).join(', ');
    const healthAlert = text => (text.match(/Service health could not be read:.{0,80}/) || [''])[0];
    const refresh = async next => { mode = next; await s.page.evaluate(() => window.__ownedHealthRefresh()); await sleep(700); };
    const metricsShown = (text, n) => text.includes(`Latency Trends (${n} queries in ring buffer)`);
    try {
      await s.page.goto(BASE + '/health', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(700);
      let text = await bodyText(s.page), list = await cards();
      const by = label => list.find(c => c.label.startsWith(label)) || {};
      r.check('a degraded 503 shows the failing service red', list.length === 3 && by('Embed').red, colours(list));
      r.check('a degraded 503 shows the services that are ok green', by('Weaviate').green && by('LLM').green, colours(list));
      r.check('a degraded 503 shows each service latency', ['11ms', '22ms', '33ms'].every(ms => text.includes(ms)), text.slice(0, 200));
      r.check('a degraded 503 is not reported as unreadable', !healthAlert(text), healthAlert(text));
      r.check('latency metrics load while health answers 503', metricsShown(text, 1), text.slice(0, 300));

      await refresh('ok'); list = await cards(); text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('a 200 shows every service green', list.length === 3 && list.every(c => c.green), colours(list));

      await refresh('proxy502'); list = await cards(); text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('an API down behind the proxy (502) shows a message',
              /Service health could not be read: The API is not responding/.test(text), text.slice(0, 300));
      r.check('a failed health load removes the earlier green cards', list.length === 0, colours(list));
      r.check('latency metrics load while the health call fails', metricsShown(text, 3), text.slice(0, 300));

      await refresh('ok'); list = await cards(); text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('the next good health load clears the message and shows the cards',
              !healthAlert(text) && list.length === 3 && list.every(c => c.green), healthAlert(text) || colours(list));

      await refresh('refused'); list = await cards(); text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('an unreachable API shows a message',
              /Service health could not be read: The API could not be reached/.test(text), text.slice(0, 300));
      r.check('an unreachable API shows no service cards', list.length === 0, colours(list));
      r.check('latency metrics load while the API is unreachable for health', metricsShown(text, 5), text.slice(0, 300));

      await refresh('html503'); list = await cards(); text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('a 503 without a health body shows a message, not cards',
              /Service health could not be read: HTTP 503/.test(text) && list.length === 0, text.slice(0, 300));
      r.check('degraded and unreachable health cause no React page errors', !s.errors.some(e => e.startsWith('pageerror:')),
              s.errors.filter(e => e.startsWith('pageerror:')).slice(0, 2).join(' | '));
    } finally { await s.ctx.close(); }
  }

  // ── owned session-recovery diagnostic HTTP fixtures ───────────────────────
  r.section('session recovery diagnostics');
  for (const failure of [false, true]) {
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'engineer');
    await s.page.setRequestInterception(true);
    s.page.on('request', async request => {
      if (new URL(request.url()).pathname === '/api/goldstandard/diagnostics') {
        return request.respond({ status: failure ? 503 : 200, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify(failure ? { error: { message: 'Synthetic diagnostic read failure' } } : { issues: [{ filename: 'gs_ownedfixture.json', code: 'SESSION_READ_FAILED', message: 'Owned unreadable snapshot preserved.' }] }) });
      }
      return request.continue();
    });
    try {
      await s.page.goto(BASE + '/health', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(500);
      const text = await bodyText(s.page);
      if (failure) {
        r.check('diagnostic refresh failure is visible', /Session recovery diagnostics could not be refreshed/.test(text));
      } else {
        r.check('retained-session recovery warning is visible on Health', /Evaluation session recovery needs attention/.test(text));
        r.check('recovery warning exposes filename, code and preservation message', /gs_ownedfixture.json/.test(text) && /SESSION_READ_FAILED/.test(text) && /Owned unreadable snapshot preserved/.test(text));
      }
      r.check('diagnostic ' + (failure ? 'failure' : 'warning') + ' does not cause React page errors', !s.errors.some(error => error.startsWith('pageerror:')));
    } finally { await s.ctx.close(); }
  }

  // Controlled refresh timing exercises visible pending, failure and ordering.
  {
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'engineer');
    await s.page.evaluateOnNewDocument(() => {
      const original = window.setInterval;
      window.setInterval = (fn, delay, ...args) => {
        if (delay === 30000) { window.__ownedHealthRefresh = fn; return 45001; }
        return original(fn, delay, ...args);
      };
    });
    const pending = [];
    await s.page.setRequestInterception(true);
    s.page.on('request', request => {
      if (new URL(request.url()).pathname === '/api/goldstandard/diagnostics') pending.push(request);
      else request.continue();
    });
    const next = async () => {
      for (let i = 0; i < 100 && !pending.length; i++) await sleep(50);
      if (!pending.length) throw new Error('Owned diagnostic refresh did not arrive');
      return pending.shift();
    };
    const respond = (request, filename, status = 200) => request.respond({ status, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify(status === 200 ? { issues: [{ filename, code: 'SESSION_READ_FAILED', message: 'Owned retained result.' }] } : { error: { message: 'Owned refresh failure' } }) });
    const refresh = () => s.page.evaluate(() => window.__ownedHealthRefresh());
    try {
      await s.page.goto(BASE + '/health', { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
      const initial = await next(); await sleep(150);
      r.check('initial diagnostic pending state is visible', /Refreshing session recovery diagnostics/.test(await bodyText(s.page)));
      await respond(initial, 'gs_previousfixture.json'); await sleep(250);
      await refresh(); const failed = await next(); await sleep(100);
      let text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('pending refresh labels retained diagnostics as previous results', /Previous evaluation session recovery results/.test(text) && /gs_previousfixture.json/.test(text));
      await respond(failed, '', 503); await sleep(250); text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('failed refresh removes old current-issue claims and clears pending state', /could not be refreshed/.test(text) && !/gs_previousfixture.json|Refreshing session recovery diagnostics/.test(text));
      await refresh(); const recovered = await next(); await respond(recovered, 'gs_currentfixture.json'); await sleep(250); text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('successful refresh clears the error and pending indicators', /gs_currentfixture.json/.test(text) && !/could not be refreshed|Refreshing session recovery diagnostics/.test(text));
      await refresh(); const older = await next(); await refresh(); const newer = await next();
      await respond(newer, 'gs_latestfixture.json'); await sleep(200);
      await respond(older, '', 503); await sleep(250); text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('late failed response cannot overwrite newer diagnostic success', /gs_latestfixture.json/.test(text) && !/could not be refreshed/.test(text));
      await refresh(); const olderSuccess = await next(); await refresh(); const newerSuccess = await next();
      await respond(newerSuccess, 'gs_finalfixture.json'); await sleep(150);
      await respond(olderSuccess, 'gs_stalefixture.json'); await sleep(250); text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('late successful response cannot replace newer diagnostic results', /gs_finalfixture.json/.test(text) && !/gs_stalefixture.json/.test(text));
      r.check('refresh error and timing fixtures do not cause React page errors', !s.errors.some(error => error.startsWith('pageerror:')));
    } finally { await s.ctx.close(); }
  }

  // Imported identities are exposed through the existing visible job notes.
  r.section('imported session lookup IDs');
  {
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'engineer');
    const filename = 'ragpkg-owned-session.tar.gz';
    const sourceId = 'gs_460abcde', localId = 'gs_460abcdf';
    const submissions = [];
    await s.page.setRequestInterception(true);
    s.page.on('request', request => {
      const path = new URL(request.url()).pathname;
      let body;
      if (path === '/api/packages') body = { packages: [{ filename, size_bytes: 100, collection: 'OwnedOriginal', chunk_count: 1, fidelity: 'chunks-only', created_at: '2026-09-28T00:00:00Z', readable: true }] };
      else if (path === '/api/import' && request.method() === 'POST') {
        submissions.push(JSON.parse(request.postData()));
        return request.respond({ status: 202, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ job_id: 'owned-identity-job', status: 'queued', filename }) });
      } else if (path === '/api/import/job/owned-identity-job') body = { job_id: 'owned-identity-job', status: 'completed', filename, on_conflict: 'rename', collection: 'OwnedImported', original_collection: 'OwnedOriginal', chunks_written: 1, fidelity: 'chunks-only', renamed: true, notes: ["evaluation session '" + sourceId + "' restored as local '" + localId + "' for 'OwnedImported'"], restored_sessions: [{ source_session_id: sourceId, session_id: localId, collection: 'OwnedImported' }], error: null, error_code: null, error_detail: null };
      if (body) return request.respond({ status: 200, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify(body) });
      return request.continue();
    });
    try {
      await s.page.goto(BASE + '/transfer', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(250);
      await s.page.evaluate(value => {
        const selector = [...document.querySelectorAll('select')].find(el => [...el.options].some(option => option.value === value));
        Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLSelectElement.prototype, 'value').set.call(selector, value);
        selector.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true }));
        document.querySelector('input[name="conflict"][value="rename"]').click();
      }, filename);
      await s.page.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].find(button => button.textContent.trim() === 'Import').click()); await sleep(600);
      const text = await bodyText(s.page);
      r.check('rename import submits selected package and explicit policy', submissions.length === 1 && submissions[0].filename === filename && submissions[0].on_conflict === 'rename');
      r.check('completed import displays original and allocated session IDs for lookup', text.includes(sourceId) && text.includes(localId) && text.includes('OwnedImported'));
      r.check('import identity notes do not cause React page errors', !s.errors.some(error => error.startsWith('pageerror:')));
    } finally { await s.ctx.close(); }
  }

  // ── transfer help page ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  r.section('transfer help page');
  {
    const s = await session(browser, BASE, 'engineer');
    await s.page.goto(BASE + '/help/transfer', { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' }); await sleep(2500);
    const info = await s.page.evaluate(() => {
      const h1 = document.querySelector('h1');
      const p = document.querySelector('article p');
      return {
        chars: (document.querySelector('#root')?.innerText || '').length,
        headings: [...document.querySelectorAll('h2')].map(e => e.textContent.trim()),
        tables: document.querySelectorAll('table').length,
        h1Size: h1 ? parseFloat(getComputedStyle(h1).fontSize) : 0,
        pSize: p ? parseFloat(getComputedStyle(p).fontSize) : 0,
      };
    });
    r.check('the help page renders substantive content', info.chars > 3000, `${info.chars} chars`);
    r.check('markdown tables render', info.tables >= 3, `${info.tables} tables`);
    r.check('headings are styled (typography plugin present)', info.h1Size > info.pSize,
            `h1=${info.h1Size}px p=${info.pSize}px`);
    for (const want of ['Where packages live', 'Naming', 'What a package contains',
                        'Fidelity', 'embedding model rule', 'name collision', 'Tuning after import']) {
      r.check(`§10 topic covered: ${want}`,
              info.headings.some(h => h.toLowerCase().includes(want.toLowerCase())),
              info.headings.join(' | ').slice(0, 80));
    }
    r.check('no console errors on the help page', s.errors.length === 0, s.errors.slice(0, 2).join(' | '));
    await s.ctx.close();
  }

  await browser.close();
  process.exit(r.summary() ? 0 : 1);
})().catch(e => { console.log('  HARNESS FAILURE: ' + e.message); process.exit(2); });
```

## 6. Packaging and Offline Distribution

Specified in `SPECIFICATIONS.md` §11. The files below are the implementation.

### api/.dockerignore

```
# Build context exclusions for the api image.
#
# The Dockerfile ends with `COPY . .`, so anything left in this directory is
# baked into the image unless excluded here.

# Python bytecode and tool caches. Platform-specific and never useful in the
# image; they also bust the `COPY . .` layer cache on every local test run.
__pycache__/
**/__pycache__/
*.py[cod]
*$py.class
*.egg-info/
.pytest_cache/
.mypy_cache/
.ruff_cache/
.coverage
htmlcov/

# A local virtualenv would shadow the image's site-packages.
.venv/
venv/
env/
ENV/

# Runtime data. UPLOAD_DIR is the named volume ingest_uploads mounted at
# /app/uploads, so anything here would be baked in and then hidden by the mount.
uploads/

# OS and editor noise
.DS_Store
**/.DS_Store
Thumbs.db
*.swp
*~

# Local environment files.
#
# NOTE: config.py sets `env_file = ".env"`, so a .env placed in this directory
# WOULD be read at runtime if it were copied in. It is excluded deliberately --
# secrets do not belong in an image layer. docker-compose.yml supplies every
# setting the API needs as explicit environment variables. If you need local
# overrides, add them to the `api` service's `environment:` block instead.
.env
.env.*

# Version control
.git
.gitignore

# Read directly by the builder; no need to ship them inside the image.
Dockerfile
.dockerignore
```

### ui/.dockerignore

```
# Build context exclusions for the ui image.
#
# The Dockerfile runs `COPY package*.json ./` -> `npm ci` -> `COPY . .`, so the
# second COPY lands on top of an already-installed tree. Without this file, a
# host node_modules/ would overwrite the container's freshly installed packages
# with ones built for the host platform (darwin/arm64 binaries inside a linux
# image), producing a broken or silently wrong build.

# Host install and build output
node_modules
dist
.vite
.cache

# OS and editor noise. These bust the `COPY . .` layer cache on every Finder
# or editor touch, forcing a needless rebuild of `npm run build`.
.DS_Store
**/.DS_Store
Thumbs.db
*.swp
*~

# Local environment files are never baked into an image.
# (Nothing in ui/src reads import.meta.env today, so the build does not need them.)
.env
.env.*

# Logs and caches
*.log
npm-debug.log*
yarn-error.log*
.npm
.eslintcache

# Version control
.git
.gitignore

# Read directly by the builder; no need to ship them inside the image.
Dockerfile
.dockerignore
```

### package.sh

Source-only archive (~1.3 MB). The target machine rebuilds the images and
re-downloads the models, so it needs internet.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Build a clean, distributable zip of this project.
#
#   bash package.sh [output.zip]
#
# Invoke with `bash package.sh` rather than `./package.sh` so the script does
# not depend on its own executable bit surviving a file transfer.
#
# What the archive contains: the files git tracks in the current commit (HEAD),
# built with `git archive`: source, Dockerfiles, compose file, both lock files
# (ui/package-lock.json and api/requirements.txt) and the docs. That is
# everything needed to rebuild the stack from scratch. Untracked and ignored
# files never go in -- offline tars, .env files, node_modules/, previous
# archives, the contents of ingest-inbox/ and exports/ -- and neither do
# uncommitted changes, so commit first. Run it in a git checkout (#384).
#
# What it deliberately does NOT contain: Docker images, the Weaviate index, and
# the Ollama model weights. Those are rebuilt or re-downloaded on the target
# machine -- roughly 8-10 GB of network traffic on first run.
#
# THE TARGET MACHINE MUST HAVE INTERNET ACCESS for this package to work.
# For an air-gapped install, use package-offline.sh instead: it ships the
# pre-built images and model weights, and needs no network on the target.
# See "Moving to another Mac" in README.md.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")"

# git archive works on the repository, so this directory must be the top level
# of a git checkout. In an extracted archive there is no repository, and in a
# subdirectory of another one git archive would take only that subtree.
TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || TOP=""
if [ -z "$TOP" ] || [ "$(cd "$TOP" && pwd -P)" != "$(pwd -P)" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: $(pwd) is not the top level of a git checkout. package.sh archives the tracked files of the current commit with git archive; run it in a clone of the repository." >&2
  exit 1
fi

OUT="${1:-rag-docker.zip}"
rm -f "$OUT"

# Tracked files only. ingest-inbox/.gitkeep and exports/.gitkeep are tracked, so
# both bind-mount targets exist on the target machine; without them Docker
# creates the directories as root and the user cannot drop files in.
git archive --format=zip -o "$OUT" HEAD

echo "Created $OUT ($(du -h "$OUT" | cut -f1))"
echo
echo "On the target Mac:"
echo "  unzip $OUT -d rag-docker && cd rag-docker"
echo "  docker compose up -d"
echo
echo "First run pulls base images, builds both services and downloads ~2.5 GB of"
echo "model weights, so the target machine needs internet access. Allow 20 GB of"
echo "Docker disk (32 GB recommended) -- see README.md."
echo
echo "No internet on the target? Use: bash package-offline.sh"
```

### package-offline.sh

Self-contained bundle (~4.6 GB) for an air-gapped target: source plus
`docker save` of all five images plus the Ollama model weights.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Build a fully self-contained OFFLINE bundle of this project.
#
#   bash package-offline.sh [output.tar]
#
# Unlike package.sh (source only, ~1.3 MB, needs the internet on first run),
# this bundle contains everything required to run with NO network access:
#
#   * the source tree: the files git tracks in the current commit (HEAD),
#     built with `git archive`, exactly as package.sh does. Untracked and
#     ignored files and uncommitted changes are left out (#384).
#   * all five Docker images, pre-built (docker save)
#   * the Ollama model weights (phi3.5 + nomic-embed-text)
#
# Measured at 4.6 GB (2.5 GB images + 2.2 GB model weights) with both models
# present. Build it on a machine where the stack already works,
# then move the file to the target Mac and run install-offline.sh there.

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

# git archive works on the repository, so this directory must be the top level
# of a git checkout. Checked first, before any image or volume is touched.
TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || TOP=""
if [ -z "$TOP" ] || [ "$(cd "$TOP" && pwd -P)" != "$(pwd -P)" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: $(pwd) is not the top level of a git checkout. package-offline.sh archives the tracked files of the current commit with git archive; run it in a clone of the repository." >&2
  exit 1
fi

OUT="${1:-rag-docker-offline.tar}"
OUT="$(cd "$(dirname "$OUT")" && pwd)/$(basename "$OUT")"   # absolute

# The MCP server is parked (see docker-compose.yml). Its image is deliberately
# NOT bundled: nothing in the stack uses it, and requiring it here would make
# packaging fail on a machine that has never built it. Re-add
# rag-docker-mcp:latest when the MCP server is brought back.
IMAGES=(
  rag-docker-api:latest
  rag-docker-ui:latest
  semitechnologies/weaviate:1.39.6
  ollama/ollama:0.3.14
  nginx:1.29-alpine
)

echo "==> Checking prerequisites"
for img in "${IMAGES[@]}"; do
  docker image inspect "$img" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || { echo "ERROR: image '$img' not found locally. Run 'docker compose build' and 'docker compose up -d' first." >&2; exit 1; }
done

# Resolve the compose project so we read the right volume.
PROJECT="$(docker compose config --format json | tr -d ' \n' | sed -n 's/^{"name":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')"
[ -n "$PROJECT" ] || PROJECT="$(basename "$PWD" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
MODELVOL="${PROJECT}_ollama_models"
docker volume inspect "$MODELVOL" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || { echo "ERROR: volume '$MODELVOL' not found. Start the stack once so the models download." >&2; exit 1; }

STAGE="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$STAGE"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$STAGE/rag-docker/offline"

echo "==> Copying source (tracked files of the current commit)"
# ingest-inbox/.gitkeep and exports/.gitkeep are tracked, so both mount targets
# exist on the target machine; without them Docker creates the directories as
# root and the user cannot drop files into ./ingest-inbox.
git archive --format=tar HEAD | ( cd "$STAGE/rag-docker" && tar xf - )

echo "==> Saving images (this is the slow part)"
docker save "${IMAGES[@]}" | gzip > "$STAGE/rag-docker/offline/images.tar.gz"

echo "==> Exporting model weights from volume '$MODELVOL'"
# Uses the ollama image itself as the tar helper: it ships /usr/bin/tar and is
# already part of the bundle, so no extra image is needed here or on the target.
docker run --rm --entrypoint sh \
  -v "$MODELVOL":/models:ro \
  -v "$STAGE/rag-docker/offline":/out \
  ollama/ollama:0.3.14 \
  -c 'tar czf /out/ollama_models.tar.gz -C /models .'

echo "==> Assembling bundle"
rm -f "$OUT"
tar cf "$OUT" -C "$STAGE" rag-docker

echo
echo "Created $OUT ($(du -h "$OUT" | cut -f1))"
echo "  images:       $(du -h "$STAGE/rag-docker/offline/images.tar.gz" | cut -f1)"
echo "  model weights:$(du -h "$STAGE/rag-docker/offline/ollama_models.tar.gz" | cut -f1)"
echo
echo "On the target Mac (no internet required):"
echo "  tar xf $(basename "$OUT") && cd rag-docker"
echo "  bash install-offline.sh"
```

### install-offline.sh

Runs on the target. Loads the images, restores the weights into the project's
volume, and starts the stack without building or pulling.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Install this project on a machine with NO internet access.
#
#   bash install-offline.sh
#
# Run it from inside the extracted bundle directory. It loads the pre-built
# Docker images, restores the Ollama model weights into the project's volume,
# and starts the stack without building or pulling anything.
#
# Requires only Docker Desktop (running) on the target Mac.

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

[ -f offline/images.tar.gz ] || { echo "ERROR: offline/images.tar.gz missing. This is the source-only package, not the offline bundle (see package-offline.sh)." >&2; exit 1; }
[ -f offline/ollama_models.tar.gz ] || { echo "ERROR: offline/ollama_models.tar.gz missing." >&2; exit 1; }

docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: Docker is not running. Start Docker Desktop and retry." >&2; exit 1; }

echo "==> Loading Docker images (no network used)"
docker load -i offline/images.tar.gz

echo "==> Restoring Ollama model weights"
# `compose run` resolves the project's ollama_models volume for us, so this does
# not depend on the directory name. The ollama image ships tar and was just
# loaded above, so no extra image needs pulling.
docker compose run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint sh \
  -v "$PWD/offline:/backup:ro" \
  ollama -c 'tar xzf /backup/ollama_models.tar.gz -C /root/.ollama && ls /root/.ollama'

echo "==> Starting the stack (--no-build: nothing is compiled or pulled)"
docker compose up -d --no-build

echo
echo "Waiting for services to report healthy..."
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  running=$(docker compose ps --services --filter status=running | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  [ "$running" = 5 ] && break
  sleep 5
done
docker compose ps

echo
echo "If all five services are up, open http://localhost:8080"
echo "Verify the models were restored (no download should occur):"
echo "  docker compose exec ollama ollama list"
```

### scripts/tests/test_package_archives.py

Host-side check that both distribution scripts hold exactly the tracked files
of `HEAD` (#384), run in a scratch git repository with `docker` stubbed.

```python
"""Distribution archives hold only the tracked files of HEAD (#384).

Host-side, no stack: each script runs in a scratch git repository, and
package-offline.sh talks to a stub `docker` first on PATH, never to a daemon.

Run: python3 scripts/tests/test_package_archives.py
"""
import os
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import tarfile
import tempfile
import unittest
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
SCRIPTS = ('package.sh', 'package-offline.sh')
REFUSAL = 'not the top level of a git checkout'
COMMITTED_README = 'Scratch project.\n'
GIT = ['git', '-c', 'user.name=Package Test', '-c', 'user.email=package-test@example.invalid',
       '-c', 'commit.gpgsign=false', '-c', 'init.defaultBranch=develop']
# The scratch repository and both scripts read no system or global (or XDG) git
# config, so a user's core.hooksPath or attributes can't change the result (#447).
GIT_ISOLATION = {'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM': '1', 'GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL': os.devnull}

# Answers what package-offline.sh asks of docker, and logs each call.
STUB_DOCKER = r'''#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "$*" >> "$STUB_DOCKER_LOG"
case "$1 $2" in
  "compose config") echo '{"name":"scratch"}' ;;
  "image inspect"|"volume inspect") ;;
  save*) printf 'stub image layers' ;;
  run*)
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
      case "$1" in -v) case "$2" in *:/out) touch "${2%:/out}/ollama_models.tar.gz" ;; esac; shift ;; esac
      shift
    done ;;
  *) echo "stub docker: unexpected call: $*" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
'''

# Untracked or ignored content that must never reach an archive.
UNTRACKED = (
    '.env', '.env.local', 'tools/.env.production', 'rag-docker-offline.tar', 'old.zip',
    'offline/images.tar.gz', '.claude/worktrees/fix-1/README.md', 'dev-docs/issue-1/analysis.md',
    '0', '.DS_Store', 'notes.txt', 'ingest-inbox/doc.pdf', 'exports/pkg.tar.gz',
)
EXECUTABLE = ('install-offline.sh', 'tools/run.sh')


def write(path, text, mode=0o644):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(text)
    path.chmod(mode)


class PackageArchiveTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(temp.cleanup)
        self.tmp = Path(temp.name).resolve()
        self.git_env = dict(os.environ, **GIT_ISOLATION)
        self.repo = self.tmp / 'project'
        self.repo.mkdir()
        for name in SCRIPTS + ('.gitignore',):
            shutil.copy(ROOT / name, self.repo / name)
        write(self.repo / 'install-offline.sh', '#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho install\n', 0o755)
        write(self.repo / 'README.md', COMMITTED_README)
        write(self.repo / 'ingest-inbox' / '.gitkeep', '')
        write(self.repo / 'exports' / '.gitkeep', '')
        write(self.repo / 'tools' / 'run.sh', '#!/usr/bin/env bash\n', 0o755)
        write(self.repo / 'tools' / 'data.txt', 'data\n')
        self.git('init', '-q')
        self.git('add', '-A')
        self.git('add', '-f', 'ingest-inbox/.gitkeep', 'exports/.gitkeep')
        self.git('commit', '-q', '-m', 'scratch')
        self.tracked = set(self.git('ls-files').split())
        for name in UNTRACKED:
            write(self.repo / name, 'must not ship\n')
        with open(self.repo / 'README.md', 'a') as handle:
            handle.write('UNCOMMITTED EDIT\n')
        self.assertEqual(set(self.git('ls-files').split()), self.tracked)
        bin_dir = self.tmp / 'bin'
        write(bin_dir / 'docker', STUB_DOCKER, 0o755)
        self.log = self.tmp / 'docker.log'
        self.env = dict(self.git_env, PATH=f'{bin_dir}{os.pathsep}{os.environ["PATH"]}',
                        STUB_DOCKER_LOG=str(self.log))

    def git(self, *args, cwd=None):
        return subprocess.run(GIT + list(args), cwd=cwd or self.repo, env=self.git_env, check=True,
                              capture_output=True, text=True).stdout

    def run_script(self, directory, script, out):
        return subprocess.run(['bash', str(directory / script), str(out)], cwd=self.tmp, env=self.env,
                              capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)

    def assert_ran(self, result):
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout + result.stderr)

    def expected_bundle(self):
        return ({'rag-docker/' + name for name in self.tracked}
                | {'rag-docker/offline/images.tar.gz', 'rag-docker/offline/ollama_models.tar.gz'})

    def assert_archives_hold_the_tracked_files(self, directory):
        zip_out, bundle_out = self.tmp / 'check.zip', self.tmp / 'check.tar'
        self.assert_ran(self.run_script(directory, 'package.sh', zip_out))
        self.assert_ran(self.run_script(directory, 'package-offline.sh', bundle_out))
        with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_out) as archive:
            self.assertEqual({i.filename for i in archive.infolist() if not i.filename.endswith('/')},
                             self.tracked)
        with tarfile.open(bundle_out) as archive:
            self.assertEqual({m.name for m in archive.getmembers() if m.isfile()}, self.expected_bundle())

    def test_zip_holds_exactly_the_tracked_files(self):
        out = self.tmp / 'out.zip'
        self.assert_ran(self.run_script(self.repo, 'package.sh', out))
        with zipfile.ZipFile(out) as archive:
            infos = {i.filename: i for i in archive.infolist() if not i.filename.endswith('/')}
            self.assertEqual(set(infos), self.tracked)
            self.assertEqual(archive.read('README.md').decode(), COMMITTED_README)
        for name in EXECUTABLE:
            with self.subTest(executable=name):
                self.assertTrue((infos[name].external_attr >> 16) & stat.S_IXUSR)

    def test_offline_bundle_holds_tracked_files_and_offline_payload(self):
        out = self.tmp / 'bundle.tar'
        self.assert_ran(self.run_script(self.repo, 'package-offline.sh', out))
        expected = {'rag-docker/' + name for name in self.tracked}
        expected |= {'rag-docker/offline/images.tar.gz', 'rag-docker/offline/ollama_models.tar.gz'}
        with tarfile.open(out) as archive:
            files = {m.name: m for m in archive.getmembers() if m.isfile()}
            self.assertEqual(set(files), expected)
            self.assertEqual(archive.extractfile('rag-docker/README.md').read().decode(), COMMITTED_README)
        for name in EXECUTABLE:
            with self.subTest(executable=name):
                self.assertTrue(files['rag-docker/' + name].mode & stat.S_IXUSR)

    def test_refuses_outside_a_git_top_level(self):
        plain = self.tmp / 'extracted'
        nested = self.repo / 'tools' / 'copy'
        for directory in (plain, nested):
            directory.mkdir(parents=True)
            for script in SCRIPTS:
                shutil.copy(ROOT / script, directory / script)
                out = self.tmp / f'{directory.name}-{script}.out'
                with self.subTest(directory=directory.name, script=script):
                    result = self.run_script(directory, script, out)
                    self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout)
                    self.assertIn(REFUSAL, result.stderr)
                    self.assertFalse(out.exists())
        calls = self.log.read_text() if self.log.exists() else ''
        self.assertEqual(calls, '', 'docker was called before the refusal')

    def test_runs_in_a_checkout_reached_through_a_symlink(self):
        link = self.tmp / 'linked'
        link.symlink_to(self.repo, target_is_directory=True)
        self.assert_archives_hold_the_tracked_files(link)

    def test_ignores_the_users_git_config(self):
        temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(temp.cleanup)
        hostile = Path(temp.name).resolve()
        marker = hostile / 'hook-ran'
        write(hostile / 'hooks' / 'pre-commit', f'#!/bin/sh\ntouch "{marker}"\nexit 1\n', 0o755)
        write(hostile / 'attributes', 'README.md export-ignore\n')
        write(hostile / 'gitconfig', f'[core]\n\thooksPath = {hostile / "hooks"}\n'
                                     f'\tattributesFile = {hostile / "attributes"}\n')
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=str(hostile / 'gitconfig')):
            # A fresh scratch repository, built while the caller's global config is hostile.
            self.setUp()
            self.assert_archives_hold_the_tracked_files(self.repo)
        self.assertIn('README.md', self.tracked)
        self.assertFalse(marker.exists(), 'the global pre-commit hook ran')


class EmbeddedCopyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_embedded_copies_match(self):
        text = (ROOT / 'IMPLEMENTATION.md').read_text()
        for name in SCRIPTS + ('scripts/verify/01_infrastructure.sh', 'scripts/verify/README.md',
                               'scripts/tests/test_package_archives.py'):
            with self.subTest(file=name):
                fence = '````' if name.endswith('.md') else '```'
                language = 'markdown' if name.endswith('.md') else 'bash' if name.endswith('.sh') else 'python'
                header = f'### {name}\n\n'
                start = text.index(header) + len(header)
                start = text.index(f'{fence}{language}\n', start) + len(fence + language) + 1
                end = text.index('\n' + fence + '\n', start)
                self.assertEqual(text[start:end], (ROOT / name).read_text().rstrip('\n'))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
```
